label: tm-notation
title: Notation and conventions
html:
This appendix is self-contained: every transfer matrix appears in explicit closed form, with notation defined locally.

Symbols are collected in Table 1. Every transfer matrix is labelled by a pair of knots (K_1, K_2) meeting at a crossing. The relevant knots and their labels are listed in Table 2. Particle assignments for each knot type are in Table 3. Knot assignments for the proton and neutron are given in Table 4.

The per-crossing transfer matrices are composed across a nucleus to produce a single scalar, its nuclear Skein polynomial P_{\mathcal{N}}(q).

Given a nucleus with A = Z + N nucleons, the braid word has A - 1 generators \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{A-2}. At each generator \sigma_i, the transfer matrices of all crossings are composed as operators acting by left-multiplication, applied from right to left in the braid word:

  M_i(q) = \prod_{j=A-1}^{i+1} T_{K_j, K_i}(q)

The product is taken in decreasing order of j. The Markov-traced volume at generator \sigma_i is

  \hat{V}_i(q) = z(q) \cdot (M_i)_{11} + (M_i)_{21}

where z(q) = q^3/(q^2+1) = q^2/[2]_q is the Markov-trace loop value — convention D (the excised convention C wrote 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), which weights the Temperley–Lieb generator e_i = q - \sigma_i at the wrong argument, not the Hecke generator \sigma_i stabilised here). Every \hat V_i(q) and hence every P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) in this appendix carries this substitution; the worked numerals downstream have not been regenerated and are still convention-C values (2026-08-09). The nuclear Skein polynomial is:

  P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) = \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q)

This requires exactly \binom{A}{2} transfer matrix multiplications.
